overviewParagraphs: Ballyshear Golf Links is Bangkok's most intellectually serious golf offering — a course built for players who understand and appreciate golf history. The design is a faithful contemporary recreation of C.B. Macdonald's legendary Lido Golf Club (1914), a Long Island layout considered among the finest classical designs ever created, and destroyed decades ago by development. Ballyshear resurrects it in Southeast Asia for a new generation of golfers.

Macdonald's design philosophy — wide corridors, multiple strategic approaches, ground game emphasis, and template holes derived from the greatest holes in golf history — is preserved faithfully throughout. Playing Ballyshear demands a different mental approach from the typical resort experience: bump-and-run, links creativity, and strategic positioning matter far more than conventional shot selection.

For discerning golfers with a deep love of classical golf architecture and a desire for something genuinely unique in Thailand's golf landscape, AGS regards Ballyshear as an extraordinary discovery. It sits in an entirely different cultural category from the resort courses that dominate the market — and that is precisely its value.

curatorBriefHtml: Ballyshear Golf Links at Ban Rakat Club (opened 2021 by acclaimed architect Gil Hanse, roughly 45 minutes east of central Bangkok) is one of Asia’s most celebrated modern architectural landmarks. Inspired by C.B. Macdonald’s legendary lost 1914 Lido Golf Club, Hanse built template holes — Redan, Biarritz, Alps, and Channel — across open, windswept links terrain measuring 6,152 yards from the Blue Tees (Par 71) with ultra-firm turf and bold geometric greens.

Operating as an invitation-only private club designed for walking purists (backed by a serene Kengo Kuma-designed clubhouse), Ballyshear is a dream ticket for architecture enthusiasts who value strategy, ground-game imagination, and historical design over resort flash.

AGS coordinates vetted weekday guest introductions at Ban Rakat Club for discerning golfers visiting Bangkok, pairing Ballyshear with Thai Country Club and Nikanti from luxury bases like Sindhorn Kempinski.

scorecard.verdict: Designed by Gil Hanse as an homage to C.B. Macdonald's legendary Lido Club. A thrilling strategic revival featuring authentic Golden Age template holes like the Biarritz, Redan, and Punchbowl.

faqs.q: Why do golf architecture fans rave about Ballyshear Golf Links?
faqs.a: Designed by Gil Hanse and inspired by C.B. Macdonald’s lost 1914 Lido Golf Club, Ballyshear brings authentic Golden Age template holes (Redan, Biarritz, Alps) and firm, strategic links shotmaking to Thailand.

faqs.q: Can international visitors play Ballyshear Golf Links (Ban Rakat Club)?
faqs.a: Ballyshear is a private members’ club with strictly limited guest access. AGS arranges vetted weekday visitor introductions well in advance as part of tailored Bangkok luxury itineraries.

faqs.q: How far is Ballyshear Golf Links from Bangkok and Suvarnabhumi Airport?
faqs.a: Located in Bang Bo (Samut Prakan), Ballyshear is just 30 minutes from Suvarnabhumi International Airport (BKK) and 45–55 minutes east of central Bangkok.

faqs.q: Is Ballyshear walkable and what makes its clubhouse special?
faqs.a: Yes — Hanse routed Ballyshear as a classic walkable links, anchored by a minimalist timber clubhouse designed by renowned Japanese architect Kengo Kuma.
